#[arg(short = 'o', long)]\n267\t        output: Option<PathBuf>,\n268\t    },\n269\t\n270\t    /// Show outcome statistics aggregated from telemetry logs.\n271\t    ///\n272\t    /// Reads JSONL #[arg(long)]\n286\t        since: Option<String>,\n287\t\n288\t        /// Include only events until this time (e.g., 1h, 24h, 7d, 2026-03-20T15:00:00Z).\n289\t        #[arg(long)]\n290\t ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n340\t// Entry point\n341\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n342\t\n343\t/// Entry point called from `main`.\n344\tpub fn run() -> Result<()> {\n345\t    let cli = Cli::parse();\n346\t\n347\t    match cli.command {\n348\t        CliCommand::Run {\n349\t            workspace,\n350\t            agent,\n351\t            count,\n352\t            identifier,\n353\t    by_worker,\n366\t            cost,\n367\t            since,\n368\t            until,\n369\t            idle_strands,\n370\t        } => cmd_status(format, by_worker, cost, since, until, }\n403\t}\n404\t\n405\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n406\t// Command handlers\n407\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n408\t\n409\t/// `needle run` — launch a worker.\n410\t///\n411\t/// Always creates dedicated tmux sessions for workers, even when invoked from\n412\t/// inside an existing tmux session. The only exception is a re-entrant inner\n413\t/// invocation launched by `launch_in_tmux()`, which is identified by the\n414\t/// `NEEDLE_INNER=1` environment variable and runs the worker directly.\n415\tfn cmd_run(\n416\t    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n417\t    agent: Option<String>,\n418\t    count: u32,\n419\t    identifier: Option<String>,\n420\t    timeout: Option<u64>,\n421\t    resume: bool,\n422\t    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n423\t) -> Result<()> {\n424\t    // Determine workspace root (CLI arg → canonicalized, else global default).\n425\t    let workspace_root = if let Some(ref ws) = workspace {\n426\t        ws.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| ws.clone())\n427\t    } else {\n428\t        let global = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n429\t        global.workspace.default.clone()\n430\t    };\n431\t\n432\t    // Load full resolved config (global → workspace .needle.yaml → env → CLI).\n433\t    let cli_overrides = CliOverrides {\n434\t        workspace: Some(workspace_root.clone()),\n435\t        agent_binary: agent.clone(),\n436\t        max_workers: None,\n437\t        ..Default::default()\n438\t    };\n439\t    let (mut config, _) = ConfigLoader::load_resolved(&workspace_root, cli_overrides)?;\n440\t\n441\t    if let Some(t) = timeout {\n442\t        config.agent.timeout = t;\n443\t    }\n444\t\n445\t    if let Some(hr) = hot_reload {\n446\t        config.self_modification.hot_reload = hr;\n447\t    }\n448\t\n449\t    if resume {\n450\t        // Hot-reload resume: inherit worker identity from --identifier,\n451\t        // load state from heartbeat file + registry, continue from SELECTING.\n452\t        let worker_id = identifier\n453\t            .clone()\n454\t            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n455\t\n456\t        // Load resume state from heartbeat and registry.\n457\t        let resume_state = crate::upgrade::ResumeState::load(&config, &worker_id)?;\n458\t\n459\t        // Emit upgrade.completed telemetry.\n460\t        let current_hash = crate::upgrade::file_hash(\n461\t            &std::env::current_exe().context(\"failed to locate own binary\")?,\n462\t        )\n463\t        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"unknown\".to_string());\n464\t\n465\t        match &resume_state {\n466\t            Some(state) => {\n467\t                tracing::info!(\n468\t                    worker = %worker_id,\n469\t                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n470\t                    beads_processed = state.beads_processed,\n471\t                    session = %state.session,\n472\t                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload\"\n473\t                );\n474\t            }\n475\t            None => {\n476\t                tracing::info!(\n477\t                    worker = %worker_id,\n478\t                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n479\t                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload (no prior state found)\"\n480\t                );\n481\t            }\n482\t        }\n483\t\n484\t        let tel = crate::telemetry::Telemetry::from_config(worker_id.clone(), &config.telemetry)\n485\t            .unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n486\t                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"hook telemetry init failed, falling back\");\n487\t                crate::telemetry::Telemetry::new(worker_id.clone())\n488\t            });\n489\t        tel.emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::UpgradeCompleted {\n490\t            new_hash: current_hash,\n491\t        })?;\n492\t\n493\t        return run_worker(config, worker_id);\n494\t    }\n495\t\n496\t    if is_needle_inner() {\n497\t        // Re-entrant inner invocation launched by launch_in_tmux() — run\n498\t        // the worker directly inside the dedicated session already created.\n499\t        let worker_id = identifier\n500\t            .clone()\n501\t            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n502\t        let agent_name = agent.as_deref().unwrap_or(&config.agent.default);\n503\t        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n504\t        tracing::info!(worker = %worker_id, session = %session_name, \"starting worker (inner re-entrant invocation)\");\n505\t        run_worker(config, worker_id)\n506\t    } else {\n507\t        // Always create dedicated tmux sessions, even if already inside tmux.\n508\t        launch_workers(\n509\t            config, workspace, agent, count, identifier, timeout, hot_reload,\n510\t        )\n511\t    }\n512\t}\n513\t\n514\t/// Launch `count` workers in separate tmux sessions with staggered startup delays.\n515\tpub fn launch_workers(\n516\t    config: Config,\n517\t    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n518\t    agent: Option<String>,\n519\t    count: u32,\n520\t    identifier: Option<String>,\n521\t    timeout: Option<u64>,\n522\t    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n523\t) -> Result<()> {\n524\t    let agent_name = agent\n525\t        .as_deref()\n526\t        .unwrap_or(&config.agent.default)\n527\t        .to_string();\n528\t    let stagger_secs = config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds;\n529\t    let max_workers = config.worker.max_workers;\n530\t\n531\t    if count == 0 {\n532\t        bail!(\"--count must be at least 1\");\n533\t    }\n534\t    if count as usize > NATO_ALPHABET.len() {\n535\t        bail!(\n536\t            \"--count {} exceeds the maximum of {} (NATO alphabet size)\",\n537\t            count,\n538\t            NATO_ALPHABET.len()\n539\t        );\n540\t    }\n541\t\n542\t    // Enforce max_workers cap (0 means unlimited).\n543\t    let effective_count = if max_workers > 0 && count > max_workers {\n544\t        tracing::warn!(\n545\t            requested = count,\n546\t            capped_to = max_workers,\n547\t            \"count exceeds max_workers; capping\"\n548\t        );\n549\t        eprintln!(\n550\t            \"Warning: --count {count} exceeds max_workers={max_workers}; launching {max_workers} workers\"\n551\t        );\n552\t        max_workers\n553\t    } else {\n554\t        count\n555\t    };\n556\t\n557\t    // --identifier is only meaningful for a single worker.\n558\t    if effective_count > 1 && identifier.is_some() {\n559\t        bail!(\"--identifier cannot be combined with --count > 1; identifiers are auto-assigned from the NATO alphabet\");\n560\t    }\n561\t\n562\t    // Detect existing sessions to avoid name collisions.\n563\t    let occupied = occupied_worker_ids(&agent_name)?;\n564\t    if !occupied.is_empty() {\n565\t        tracing::info!(\n566\t            occupied = ?occupied,\n567\t            \"found existing worker sessions\"\n568\t        );\n569\t    }\n570\t\n571\t    // Reject --identifier collision early.\n572\t    if let Some(ref id) = identifier {\n573\t        if occupied.contains(id) {\n574\t            bail!(\n575\t                \"worker '{}' is already running in session 'needle-{}-{}'\",\n576\t                id,\n577\t                agent_name,\n578\t                id\n579\t            );\n580\t        }\n581\t    }\n582\t\n583\t    // Build the list of worker IDs, skipping occupied names.\n584\t    let worker_ids: Vec<String> = if effective_count == 1 {\n585\t        vec![identifier.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {\n586\t            // Pick the first available NATO name.\n587\t            NATO_ALPHABET\n588\t                .iter()\n589\t                .find(|name| !occupied.contains(**name))\n590\t                .map(|s| s.to_string())\n591\t                .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string())\n592\t        })]\n593\t    } else {\n594\t        let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(effective_count as usize);\n595\t        for name in NATO_ALPHABET {\n596\t            if ids.len() >= effective_count as usize {\n597\t                break;\n598\t            }\n599\t            if occupied.contains(*name) {\n600\t                tracing::warn!(\n601\t                    worker_id = %name,\n602\t                    \"skipping occupied worker name\"\n603\t                );\n604\t                continue;\n605\t            }\n606\t            ids.push(name.to_string());\n607\t        }\n608\t        if ids.len() < effective_count as usize {\n609\t            bail!(\n610\t                \"cannot launch {} workers — only {} NATO names available ({} occupied)\",\n611\t                effective_count,\n612\t                ids.len(),\n613\t                occupied.len()\n614\t            );\n615\t        }\n616\t        ids\n617\t    };\n618\t\n619\t    for (seq, worker_id) in worker_ids.iter().enumerate() {\n620\t        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n621\t\n622\t        tracing::info!(\n623\t            worker_id = %worker_id,\n624\t            sequence = seq,\n625\t            total = effective_count,\n626\t            session = %session_name,\n627\t            \"launching worker\"\n628\t        );\n629\t\n630\t        // Stagger: sleep before launching subsequent workers.\n631\t        if seq > 0 && stagger_secs > 0 {\n632\t            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(stagger_secs));\n633\t        }\n634\t\n635\t        launch_in_tmux(\n636\t            &session_name,\n637\t            workspace.clone(),\n638\t            agent.clone(),\n639\t            Some(worker_id.clone()),\n640\t            timeout,\n641\t            hot_reload,\n642\t        )?;\n643\t\n644\t        println!(\n645\t            \"[{}/{}] Started worker '{}' in tmux session: {session_name}\",\n646\t            seq + 1,\n647\t            effective_count,\n648\t            worker_id\n649\t        );\n650\t    }\n651\t\n652\t    let sanitized_agent = sanitize_session_name(&agent_name);\n653\t    if effective_count > 1 {\n654\t        println!(\n655\t            \"\\nStarted {effective_count} workers (stagger: {stagger_secs}s between launches).\"\n656\t        );\n657\t        println!(\"Attach to a worker with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-<name>\");\n658\t    } else {\n659\t        let worker_id = &worker_ids[0];\n660\t        println!(\"Attach with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-{worker_id}\");\n661\t    }\n662\t\n663\t    Ok(())\n664\t}\n665\t\n666\t/// Initialize the tracing subscriber with OTLP layer if configured.\n667\t///\n668\t/// This must be called before any tracing spans are created so that the OTLP\n669\t/// layer can export them to the configured collector.\n670\t///\n671\t/// Note: Shutdown is handled by the OtlpSink in the telemetry module, not here.\n672\t#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n673\tfn init_tracing_subscriber(\n674\t    worker_id: String,\n675\t    session_id: String,\n676\t    config: &crate::config::Config,\n677\t) -> Result<()> {\n678\t    use opentelemetry::trace::TracerProvider;\n679\t    use tracing_subscriber::{layer::SubscriberExt, util::SubscriberInitExt};\n680\t\n681\t    let use_ansi = use_ansi();\n682\t\n683\t    // Check if OTLP is enabled\n684\t    if !config.telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled {\n685\t        // No OTLP - just initialize with fmt layer\n686\t        let fmt_layer = tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n687\t            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n688\t            .with_ansi(use_ansi);\n689\t        tracing_subscriber::registry()\n690\t            .with(fmt_layer)\n691\t            .try_init()\n692\t            .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber\")?;\n693\t        return Ok(());\n694\t    }\n695\t\n696\t    // OTLP is enabled - create the OTLP layer inline\n697\t    // We create it inline to avoid type erasure issues with boxed layers\n698\t    let otlp_config = &config.telemetry.otlp_sink;\n699\t\n700\t    // Build resource attributes\n701\t    let resource = crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_resource(\n702\t        &worker_id,\n703\t        &session_id,\n704\t        otlp_config,\n705\t        Some(&config.agent.default),\n706\t        None, // model - not available in AgentConfig\n707\t        config.workspace.default.to_str(),\n708\t    )\n709\t    .context(\"failed to build OTel resource\")?;\n710\t\n711\t    // Create drop channel for tracing layer\n712\t    let (drop_tx, mut drop_rx) =\n713\t        tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel::<crate::telemetry::otlp::DropEvent>();\n714\t    tokio::spawn(async move {\n715\t        while let Some(drop) = drop_rx.recv().await {\n716\t            tracing::warn!(\n717\t                signal = drop.signal.as_str(),\n718\t                dropped_count = drop.dropped_count,\n719\t                \"OTLP tracing layer export failure\"\n720\t            );\n721\t        }\n722\t    });\n723\t\n724\t    // Build exporters and tracer provider based on protocol\n725\t    let (tracer_provider, ..) = match otlp_config.protocol.as_str() {\n726\t        \"grpc\" => {\n727\t            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_grpc_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n728\t        }\n729\t        \"http\" | \"http/protobuf\" => {\n730\t            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_http_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n731\t        }\n732\t        other => anyhow::bail!(\"invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'\"),\n733\t    };\n734\t\n735\t    // Create the OpenTelemetry tracing layer\n736\t    let otlp_layer = tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(tracer_provider.tracer(\"needle\"));\n737\t\n738\t    // Create a fmt layer that works with any subscriber implementing LookupSpan\n739\t    // We build this after the OTLP layer to ensure proper type compatibility\n740\t    let subscriber = tracing_subscriber::registry().with(otlp_layer).with(\n741\t        tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n742\t            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n743\t            .with_ansi(use_ansi),\n744\t    );\n745\t\n746\t    subscriber\n747\t        .try_init()\n748\t        .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber with OTLP\")?;\n749\t\n750\t    Ok(())\n751\t}\n752\t\n753\t/// No-op tracing initialization when OTLP feature is disabled.\n754\t#[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\n755\tfn The caller may\n/// choose to emit a failure event and continue rather than blocking.\n#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]\n#[error(\"SYNC_CONFLICT recovery failed: {reason}\")]\npub struct SyncRecoveryError {\n    pub reason: String,\n}\n\n// ─── Filters ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Filters applied when listing ready beads.\n#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]\npub struct Filters {\n    /// Only return beads assigned to this actor. `None` = no filter.\n    pub assignee: Option<String>,\n    /// Exclude beads that have any of these labels.\n    pub exclude_labels: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n// ─── RepairReport ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Summary from `br doctor --repair`.\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\npub struct RepairReport {\n    pub warnings: Vec<String>,\n    pub fixed: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n// ─── BeadStore trait ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Abstract interface to the bead backend.\n#[async_trait]\npub trait BeadStore: Send + Sync {\n    /// List all beads with no incomplete blockers (ready to work on).\n    ///\n    /// Returns an empty `Vec` when the queue is empty — that is not an error.\n    /// Returns `Err` if JSON parsing or br invocation fails.\n    async fn ready(&self, filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>>;\n\n    /// List ALL beads in the workspace (no readiness/filter checks).\n    ///\n    /// Used by Knot strand for three-state verification — a DIFFERENT code\n    /// path from `ready()` to avoid v1's false-positive bug.\n    async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>>;\n\n    /// Fetch a single bead by ID.\n    async fn show(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead>;\n\n    /// Attempt to atomically claim a bead (set status=in_progress, assignee=actor).\n    ///\n    /// Returns a `ClaimResult` describing the outcome:\n    /// - Two workers calling this simultaneously will\n    /// always receive distinct beads.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a `ClaimResult` describing the outcome:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)` — success, returns the full bead.\n    /// - `NotClaimable { reason }` — no beads available to claim.\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>;\n\n    /// Release a claimed bead back to open (e.g., after agent failure).\n    async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush local bead changes to JSONL before release.\n    ///\n    /// Runs `br sync --flush-only` to ensure any local writes are persisted\n    /// to JSONL before attempting to release a bead. install beads_rust\")?;\n        Ok(BrCliBeadStore { br_path, workspace })\n    }\n\n    /// Default timeout for br subprocess calls (30 seconds).\n    const DEFAULT_BR_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 30;\n\n    /// Run a `br` subcommand in the workspace directory and return stdout.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Err` if the process fails to spawn, exits non-zero (unless\n    /// the caller handles specific codes), or stdout is not valid UTF-8.\n    async fn run_br(&self, args: &[&str]) -> Result<String> {\n        self.run_br_in(&self.workspace, args, Self::DEFAULT_BR_TIMEOUT_SECS)\n            .await\n    }\n\n    /// Run a `br` subcommand with a custom timeout.\n    ///\n    /// Use this for calls that may take longer (e.g., sync operations).\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    async fn run_br_with_timeout(&self, args: &[&str], timeout_secs: u64) -> Result<String> {\n        self.run_br_in(&self.workspace, args, timeout_secs).await\n    }\n\n    async fn run_br_in(&self, dir: &Path, args: &[&str], timeout_secs: u64) -> Result<String> {\n        let timeout_duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs);\n\n        // kill_on_drop ensures the process is killed if the wait_with_output\n        // future is dropped (e.g., on timeout), preventing orphaned br processes.\n        let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path);\n        cmd.args(args)\n            .current_dir(dir)\n            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .kill_on_drop(true);\n        let child = cmd\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn br subprocess: {args:?}\"))?;\n\n        // Wait for output with timeout. On timeout, kill_on_drop fires automatically.\n        let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout_duration, child.wait_with_output()).await {\n            Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                return Err(e).context(format!(\"br subprocess failed: {args:?}\"));\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    timeout_secs,\n                    \"br subprocess timed out, killing process\"\n                );\n                bail!(\"br subprocess timed out after {timeout_secs}s: {args:?}\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8(output.stdout).context(\"br stdout was not valid UTF-8\")?;\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).into_owned();\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            let code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n\n            // FrankenSQLite crash recovery: if br was killed by a signal\n            // (code() returns None) but stdout shows the operation completed\n            // and stderr is empty, treat as success. This commonly happens\n            // when br's SQLite layer crashes during post-commit cleanup while\n            // the mutation was already persisted to the append-only JSONL file.\n            if output.status.code().is_none() && stderr.is_empty() && !stdout.is_empty() {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    stdout = %stdout.trim(),\n                    \"br was killed by signal but stdout indicates success — \\\n                     treating as successful (FrankenSQLite crash recovery)\"\n                );\n                return Ok(stdout);\n            }\n\n            // Auto-recover from SYNC_CONFLICT: run `br sync` then retry once.\n            if is_sync_conflict(&stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    \"br hit SYNC_CONFLICT, running br sync and retrying\"\n                );\n\n                let sync_timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(60);\n                let mut sync_cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path);\n                sync_cmd\n                    .args([\"sync\"])\n                    .current_dir(dir)\n                    .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                    .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                    .kill_on_drop(true);\n                let sync_child = sync_cmd\n                    .spawn()\n                    .context(\"failed to spawn br sync during SYNC_CONFLICT recovery\")?;\n\n                let sync_output = match tokio::time::timeout(\n                    sync_timeout,\n                    sync_child.wait_with_output(),\n                )\n                .await\n                {\n                    Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        return Err(e).context(\"br sync failed during SYNC_CONFLICT recovery\");\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::error!(\"br sync timed out after 60s during SYNC_CONFLICT recovery, killing process\");\n                        bail!(\"br sync timed out after 60s during SYNC_CONFLICT recovery\");\n                    }\n                };\n\n                if !sync_output.status.success() {\n                    let sync_stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&sync_output.stderr);\n                    tracing::warn!(stderr = %sync_stderr, \"br sync failed, retrying original command anyway\");\n                }\n\n                // Retry the original command once with timeout.\n                let mut retry_cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path);\n                retry_cmd\n                    .args(args)\n                    .current_dir(dir)\n                    .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                    .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                    .kill_on_drop(true);\n                let retry_child = retry_cmd\n                    .spawn()\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn br retry with args: {args:?}\"))?;\n\n                let retry =\n                    match tokio::time::timeout(timeout_duration, retry_child.wait_with_output())\n                        .await\n                    {\n                        Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n                        Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                            return Err(e).context(format!(\"br retry failed: {args:?}\"));\n                        }\n                        Err(_) => {\n                            tracing::error!(\n                                args = ?args,\n                                timeout_secs,\n                                \"br retry timed out, killing process\"\n                            );\n                            bail!(\"br retry subprocess timed out after {timeout_secs}s: {args:?}\");\n                        }\n                    };\n\n                let retry_stdout = String::from_utf8(retry.stdout)\n                    .context(\"br retry stdout was not valid UTF-8\")?;\n                let retry_stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&retry.stderr).into_owned();\n\n                if !retry.status.success() {\n                    let retry_code = retry.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n                    return Err(anyhow::Error::new(SyncRecoveryError {\n                        reason: format!(\n                            \"exit code {retry_code} after br sync retry\\n\\\n                             stderr: {retry_stderr}\\nstdout: {retry_stdout}\"\n                        ),\n                    }));\n                }\n\n                return Ok(retry_stdout);\n            }\n\n            bail!(\"br {args:?} exited with code {code}\\nstderr: {stderr}\\nstdout: {stdout}\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(stdout)\n    }\n\n    /// Run br and return both exit code and stdout (for claim race detection).\n    ///\n    /// Auto-recovers from SYNC_CONFLICT (exit code 6): runs `br sync` then\n    /// retries the original command once.\n    async fn run_br_with_status(&self, args: &[&str]) -> Result<(i32, String)> {\n        let timeout_duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(Self::DEFAULT_BR_TIMEOUT_SECS);\n\n        // kill_on_drop ensures the process is killed if the wait_with_output\n        // future is dropped (e.g., on timeout), preventing orphaned br processes.\n        let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path);\n        cmd.args(args)\n            .current_dir(&self.workspace)\n            .kill_on_drop(true);\n        let child = cmd\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn br subprocess: {args:?}\"))?;\n\n        let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout_duration, child.wait_with_output()).await {\n            Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                return Err(e).context(format!(\"br subprocess failed: {args:?}\"));\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    args = ?args,\n out after {timeout_secs}s: {args:?}\",\n                    timeout_secs = Self::DEFAULT_BR_TIMEOUT_SECS\n                );\n            }\n        };\n\n        let code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8(output.stdout).context(\"br stdout was not valid UTF-8\")?;\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n\n        // Auto-recover from SYNC_CONFLICT: run `br sync` then retry once.\n        if code != 0 && is_sync_conflict(&stderr) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                args = ?args,\n                \"br hit SYNC_CONFLICT (run_br_with_status), running br sync and retrying\"\n            );\n            let sync_timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(60);\n            let _ = tokio::time::timeout(\n                sync_timeout,\n                tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path)\n                    .args([\"sync\"])\n                    .current_dir(&self.workspace)\n                    .output(),\n            )\n            .await;\n\n            let retry = tokio::time::timeout(\n                timeout_duration,\n                tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path)\n                    .args(args)\n                    .current_dir(&self.workspace)\n                    .output(),\n            )\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"br retry subprocess timed out after {timeout_secs}s: {args:?}\",\n                    timeout_secs = Self::DEFAULT_BR_TIMEOUT_SECS\n                )\n            })?\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn br retry with args: {args:?}\"))?;\n\n            let retry_code = retry.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n            let retry_stdout =\n                String::from_utf8(retry.stdout).context(\"br retry stdout was not valid UTF-8\")?;\n            return Ok((retry_code, retry_stdout));\n        }\n\n        Ok((code, stdout))\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a JSON array or JSONL stream of beads from br output.\n    fn parse_beads(json: &str, context: &str) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        if json.trim().is_empty() {\n            return Ok(vec![]);\n        }\n        // Try JSON array first, then fall back to JSONL (one object per line)\n        if let Ok(beads) = serde_json::from_str::<Vec<Bead>>(json) {\n            return Ok(beads);\n        }\n        json.lines()\n            .filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty())\n            .map(|line| {\n                serde_json::from_str::<Bead>(line)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"JSON parse error from {context}:\\n{line}\"))\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a single bead from a JSON array (first element).\n    fn parse_single_bead(json: &str, context: &str) -> Result<Bead> {\n        let beads = Self::parse_beads(json, context)?;\n        beads\n            .into_iter()\n            .next()\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"{context} returned empty array\"))\n    }\n\n    /// Run `bf claim` for atomic bead selection and claiming.\n    ///\n    /// This uses bead-forge's atomic claim which performs scoring\n    /// (downstream_impact + critical_float + priority + created_at) and\n    /// the UPDATE in a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction.\n    async fn run_bf_claim(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<String> {\n        let timeout_duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(30);\n\n        // Try to find bf on PATH or at the default install location\n        let bf_path = which::which(\"bf\").or_else(|_| {\n            let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_default();\n            let candidate = PathBuf::from(format!(\"{home}/.local/bin/bf\"));\n            if candidate.exists() {\n                Ok(candidate)\n            } else {\n                Err(anyhow!(\"bf not found on PATH or at ~/.local/bin/bf\"))\n            }\n        });\n\n        let bf_path = match bf_path {\n            Ok(p) => p,\n            Err(e) => {\n                return Err(e.context(\"bf CLI not found; falling back to br-style claim\"));\n            }\n        };\n\n        let args = [\"claim\", \"--assignee\", actor, \"--json\"];\n        let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&bf_path);\n        cmd.args(args)\n            .current_dir(&self.workspace)\n            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .kill_on_drop(true);\n\n        let child = cmd\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn bf subprocess: {:?}\", args))?;\n\n        let output = match subprocess failed: {:?}\", args));\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    \"bf subprocess timed out, killing code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n            bail!(\n                \"bf {:?} exited with code {}\\nstderr: {}\",\n                args,\n                code,\n                stderr\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(stdout)\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl BeadStore for BrCliBeadStore {\n    async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let stdout = self\n fn ready(&self, filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let mut args = vec![\"ready\", \"--json\"];\n\n        // Build filter args — stored so they live long enough for the slice.\n        let assignee_arg;\n        if let Some(ref assignee) = filters.assignee {\n            args.push(\"--assignee\");\n            assignee_arg = assignee.clone();\n            args.push(&assignee_arg);\n        }\n\n        let stdout = self.run_br(&args).await.context(\"br ready failed\")?;\n        let mut beads = Self::parse_beads(&stdout, \"br ready --json\")?;\n\n        // Apply label exclusion async fn claim(&self, id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        // Attempt claim by setting status=in_progress and assignee.\n        let (code, _stdout) = self\n            .run_br_with_status(&[\n                \"update\",\n                id_str,\n                \"--status\",\n                \"in_progress\",\n                \"--assignee\",\n                actor,\n            ])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"br update {id_str} (claim) failed to spawn\"))?;\n\n        match code {\n            0 => {\n                // Verify we actually won by reading back the bead.\n                let bead = self.show(id).await?;\n                if bead.assignee.as_deref() == Some(actor) {\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead))\n                } else {\n                    let claimed_by = bead\n                        .assignee\n                        .clone()\n                        .unwrap_or_else(|| \"(unknown)\".to_string());\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost { claimed_by })\n                }\n            }\n            4 => {\n                // br exit code 4 signals a conflict / optimistic lock failure.\n                let bead = self.show(id).await.ok();\n                let claimed_by = bead\n                    .and_then(|b| b.assignee)\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| \"(unknown)\".to_string());\n                Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost { claimed_by })\n            }\n            _ => Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: blocked_id (child blocks parent)\n        // br dep add <ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON> --type blocks\n        // ISSUE depends on DEPENDS_ON, so blocked_id depends on blocker_id\n        let blocker = blocker_id.as_ref();\n        let blocked = blocked_id.as_ref();\n        self.run_br(&[\"dep\", \"add\", blocked, blocker, \"--type\", \"blocks\"])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"br dep add {blocked} {blocker} --type blocks failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn remove_dependency(&self, blocked_id: &BeadId, blocker_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        // Remove the dependency: blocked_id depends on blocker_id\n        // br dep remove <ISSUE> <DEPENDENCY>\n        let blocked = blocked_id.as_ref();\n        let blocker = blocker_id.as_ref();\n        self.run_br(&[\"dep\", \"remove\", blocked, blocker])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"br dep remove {blocked} {blocker} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn doctor_repair(&self) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n        let stdout = self\n            .run_br(&[\"doctor\", \"--repair\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"br doctor --repair failed\")?;\n        Ok(Self::parse_doctor_output(&stdout))\n    }\n\n    async fn doctor_check(&self) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n        let stdout = self.run_br(&[\"doctor\"]).await.context(\"br doctor failed\")?;\n        Ok(Self::parse_doctor_output(&stdout))\n    }\n\n    async fn full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let db_path = self.workspace.join(\".beads/beads.db\");\n\n        // Step 1: Remove the corrupt SQLite database.\n        if db_path.exists() {\n            tokio::fs::remove_file(&db_path)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to remove {}\", db_path.display()))?;\n            tracing::info!(path = %db_path.display(), \"removed corrupt database file\");\n        }\n\n        // Also remove WAL and SHM files if present.\n        for suffix in &[\"-wal\", \"-shm\"] {\n            let wal_path = self.workspace.join(format!(\".beads/beads.db{suffix}\"));\n            if wal_path.exists() {\n                let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(&wal_path).await;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Reimport from JSONL.\n        self.run_br(&[\"sync\", \"--import-only\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"br sync --import-only failed during full rebuild\")?;\n\n        // Step 3: Verify with br doctor.\n        let verify = self\n            .run_br(&[\"doctor\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"br doctor verification failed after rebuild\")?;\n        let report = Self::parse_doctor_output(&verify);\n\n        if !report.warnings.is_empty() {\n            bail!(\n                \"database still has issues after rebuild: {:?}\",\n                report.warnings\n            );\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\"database fully rebuilt from JSONL — verified clean\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        // Use bf claim's atomic select-score-update to eliminate TOCTOU race.\n        // bf claim performs scoring (downstream_impact + critical_float + priority)\n        // and the UPDATE in a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, guaranteeing\n        // that concurrent workers receive distinct beads.\n        match self.run_bf_claim(actor).await {\n            Ok(stdout) => {\n                // bf claim returns JSON with bead_id or empty object for no candidates\n                let trimmed = stdout.trim();\n                if trimmed.is_empty() || trimmed == \"{}\" || trimmed == \"null\" {\n                    return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                        reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                    });\n                }\n\n                // Parse the JSON response from bf claim\n                #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]\n                struct BfClaimResponse {\n                    bead_id: Option<String>,\n                    #[allow(dead_code)]\n                    assignee: Option<String>,\n                }\n\n                let response: BfClaimResponse = serde_json::from_str(trimmed)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"bf claim returned invalid JSON: {}\", trimmed))?;\n\n                if let Some(bead_id) = response.bead_id {\n                    // Fetch the full bead details\n                    self.show(&BeadId::from(bead_id))\n                        .await\n                        .map(ClaimResult::Claimed)\n                } else {\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                        reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                    })\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // If bf is not available, fall back to the old br-style pattern\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"bf claim failed, falling back to br-style ready+claim\");\n                let filters = Filters::default();\n                let candidates = self.ready(&filters).await?;\n                if let Some(bead) = candidates.first() {\n                    self.claim(&bead.id, actor).await\n                } else {\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                        reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                    })\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl BrCliBeadStore {\n    /// Parse `br doctor` output into a `RepairReport`.\n    fn parse_doctor_output(stdout: &str) -> RepairReport {\n        let mut report = RepairReport::default();\n        for line in stdout.lines() {\n            if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(\"WARN \") {\n                // Filter out non-actionable warnings that cannot be repaired\n                // (e.g., sqlite3 binary not installed on the system, or\n                // leftover recovery backup files from a prior repair/rebuild).\n                if rest.contains(\"sqlite3 not available\") || rest.contains(\"recovery_artifacts\") {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                report.warnings.push(rest.to_string());\n            } else if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(\"FIXED \") {\n                report.fixed.push(rest.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n        report\n    }\n\n    /// Attempt database recovery: try repair first, then full rebuild.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the outcome of the recovery attempt. This is the primary\n    /// entry point for auto-recovery from SQLite corruption.\n    pub async fn recover_db(&self) -> RecoveryOutcome {\n        // Step 1: Try br doctor --repair.\n        tracing::warn!(\"attempting database recovery via br doctor --repair\");\n        match self.doctor_repair().await {\n            Ok(report) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    warnings = report.warnings.len(),\n                    fixed = report.fixed.len(),\n                    \"br doctor --repair completed\"\n                );\n                return RecoveryOutcome::Repaired(report);\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"br doctor --repair failed, attempting full rebuild\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Full rebuild — rm db + br sync --import + verify.\n        match self.full_rebuild().await {\n            Ok(()) => RecoveryOutcome::Rebuilt,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::error!(error = %e, \"full database rebuild failed — JSONL may be corrupt\");\n                RecoveryOutcome::Failed(e)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── BfCliBeadStore ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// `bf` CLI-backed bead store implementation.\n///\n/// Uses `bf claim` for atomic server-selected bead claiming. This eliminates\n/// the race condition in `BrCliBeadStore.claim()` where two workers could both\n/// see the same bead in `ready()` and race to claim it.\n///\n/// The key difference: `bf claim` atomically selects AND claims a bead in a\n/// single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, guaranteeing that concurrent workers\n/// receive distinct beads.\npub struct BfCliBeadStore {\n    /// Path to the `bf` binary.\n    pub bf_path: PathBuf,\n    /// Workspace root (directory containing `.beads/`).\n    pub workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Model name for telemetry (e.g., \"claude-opus-4-7\").\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n    /// Harness name for telemetry (e.g., \"needle\").\n    pub harness: Option<String>,\n    /// Harness version for telemetry.\n    pub harness_version: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl BfCliBeadStore {\n    /// Construct a new store, validating that the `bf` binary exists.\n    pub fn new(\n        bf_path: PathBuf,\n        workspace: PathBuf,\n        model: Option<String>,\n        harness: Option<String>,\n        harness_version: Option<String>,\n    ) -> Result<Self> {\n        if !bf_path.exists() {\n            bail!(\"bf binary not found at {}\", bf_path.display());\n        }\n        Ok(BfCliBeadStore {\n            bf_path,\n            workspace,\n            model,\n            harness,\n            harness_version,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Try to find `bf` on PATH or the default install location.\n    pub fn discover(\n        workspace: PathBuf,\n        model: Option<String>,\n        harness: Option<String>,\n        harness_version: Option<String>,\n    ) -> Result<Self> {\n        let bf_path = which::which(\"bf\")\n            .or_else(|_| {\n                let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_default();\n                let candidate = PathBuf::from(format!(\"{home}/.local/bin/bf\"));\n                if candidate.exists() {\n                    Ok(candidate)\n                } else {\n                    Err(anyhow!(\"bf not found on PATH or at ~/.local/bin/bf\"))\n                }\n            })\n            .context(\"bf CLI not found; install bead-forge\")?;\n        Ok(BfCliBeadStore {\n            bf_path,\n            workspace,\n            model,\n            harness,\n            harness_version,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Default timeout for bf subprocess calls (30 seconds).\n    const DEFAULT_BF_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 30;\n\n    /// Run a `bf` subcommand in the workspace directory and return stdout.\n    async fn run_bf(&self, args: &[&str]) -> Result<String> {\n        self.run_bf_in(&self.workspace, args, Self::DEFAULT_BF_TIMEOUT_SECS)\n            .await\n    }\n\n    async fn run_bf_in(&self, dir: &Path, args: &[&str], timeout_secs: u64) -> Result<String> {\n        let timeout_duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs);\n\n        let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.bf_path);\n        cmd.args(args)\n            .current_dir(dir)\n            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .kill_on_drop(true);\n        let child = cmd\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn bf subprocess: {args:?}\"))?;\n\n        let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout_duration, child.wait_with_output()).await {\n            Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                return Err(e).context(format!(\"bf subprocess failed: {args:?}\"));\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    timeout_secs,\n                    \"bf subprocess timed out, killing process\"\n                );\n                bail!(\"bf subprocess timed out after {timeout_secs}s: {args:?}\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8(output.stdout).context(\"bf stdout was not valid UTF-8\")?;\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            let code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n            bail!(\"bf {args:?} exited with code {code}\\nstderr: {stderr}\\nstdout: {stdout}\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(stdout)\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a JSON array of beads from bf output.\n    /// Handles both JSON array format `[{...},{...}]` and NDJSON (one object per line).\n    fn parse_beads(json: &str, context: &str) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let trimmed = json.trim();\n        if trimmed.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(vec![]);\n        }\n        // Try JSON array first (bf show returns [...])\n        if trimmed.starts_with('[') {\n            return serde_json::from_str::<Vec<Bead>>(trimmed)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"JSON parse error from {context}:\\n{json}\"));\n        }\n        // Fall back to NDJSON (bf list returns one object per line)\n        let mut beads = Vec::new();\n        for line in trimmed.lines() {\n            let line = line.trim();\n            if line.is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let bead: Bead = serde_json::from_str(line)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"NDJSON parse error from {context}: {line}\"))?;\n            beads.push(bead);\n        }\n        Ok(beads)\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a single bead from a JSON array (first element).\n    fn parse_single_bead(json: &str, context: &str) -> Result<Bead> {\n        let beads = Self::parse_beads(json, context)?;\n        beads\n            .into_iter()\n            .next()\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"{context} returned empty array\"))\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl BeadStore for BfCliBeadStore {\n    async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let stdout = self\n            .run_bf(&[\"list\", \"--json\", \"--limit\", \"0\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"bf list --json failed\")?;\n        Self::parse_beads(&stdout, \"bf list --json\")\n    }\n\n    async fn ready(&self, filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let mut args = vec![\"list\", \"--json\", \"--status\", \"open\", \"--limit\", \"0\"];\n\n        // Build filter args — stored so they live long enough for the slice.\n        let assignee_arg;\n        if let Some(ref assignee) = filters.assignee {\n            args.push(\"--assignee\");\n            assignee_arg = assignee.clone();\n            args.push(&assignee_arg);\n        }\n\n        let stdout = self.run_bf(&args).await.context(\"bf list failed\")?;\n        let mut beads = Self::parse_beads(&stdout, \"bf list --json\")?;\n\n        // Apply label exclusion filter (bf CLI doesn't support this natively).\n        if !filters.exclude_labels.is_empty() {\n            beads.retain(|b| !b.labels.iter().any(|l| filters.exclude_labels.contains(l)));\n        }\n\n        Ok(beads)\n    }\n\n    async fn show(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        let stdout = self\n            .run_bf(&[\"show\", id_str, \"--json\"])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf show {id_str} failed\"))?;\n        Self::parse_single_bead(&stdout, &format!(\"bf show {id_str} --json\"))\n    }\n\n    async fn claim(&self, _id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        // BfCliBeadStore uses atomic claim_auto() for all claim operations.\n        // This eliminates the race condition from the old br-style\n        // \"update + show verify\" pattern — two workers racing to claim\n        // the same bead will always receive distinct beads.\n        self.claim_auto(actor).await\n    }\n\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        // Build bf claim args\n        let mut args = vec![\"claim\", \"--assignee\", actor, \"--json\"];\n\n        // Optional telemetry args\n        let model_arg;\n        let harness_arg;\n        let harness_version_arg;\n\n        if let Some(ref model) = self.model {\n            args.push(\"--model\");\n            model_arg = model.as_str();\n            args.push(model_arg);\n        }\n        if let Some(ref harness) = self.harness {\n            args.push(\"--harness\");\n            harness_arg = harness.as_str();\n            args.push(harness_arg);\n        }\n        if let Some(ref harness_version) = self.harness_version {\n            args.push(\"--harness-version\");\n            harness_version_arg = harness_version.as_str();\n            args.push(harness_version_arg);\n        }\n\n        let stdout = self.run_bf(&args).await.context(\"bf claim failed\")?;\n\n        // Parse JSON output: {\"bead_id\": \"...\", \"reclaimed\": 0, \"assignee\": \"...\"}\n        let json: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&stdout)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf claim returned invalid JSON: {stdout}\"))?;\n\n        if let Some(bead_id) = json.get(\"bead_id\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n            if bead_id.is_empty() || stdout.contains(\"No beads available\") {\n                return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                    reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            // Fetch the full bead details\n            let bead = self.show(&BeadId::from(bead_id)).await?;\n            Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead))\n        } else {\n            Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n            })\n        }\n    }\n\n    async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"update\", id_str, \"--status\", \"open\", \"--assignee\", \"\"])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf release {id_str} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn flush(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        self.run_bf(&[\"sync\", \"--flush-only\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"bf sync --flush-only failed\")?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn reopen(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"reopen\", id_str])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf reopen {id_str} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn labels(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        let bead = self.show(id).await?;\n        Ok(bead.labels)\n    }\n\n    async fn add_label(&self, id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"label\", \"add\", id_str, \"--label\", label])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf label add {id_str} {label} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn remove_label(&self, id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"label\", \"remove\", id_str, \"--label\", label])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf label remove {id_str} {label} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn create_bead(&self, title: &str, body: &str, labels: &[&str]) -> Result<BeadId> {\n        let mut args: Vec<String> = vec![\n            \"create\".into(),\n            \"--title\".into(),\n            title.into(),\n            \"--description\".into(),\n            body.into(),\n        ];\n        for label in labels {\n            args.push(\"--label\".into());\n            args.push((*label).into());\n        }\n        let arg_refs: Vec<&str> = args.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n        let stdout = self.run_bf(&arg_refs).await.context(\"bf create failed\")?;\n        let id_str = stdout.trim();\n        if id_str.is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"bf create returned empty ID\");\n        }\n        Ok(BeadId::from(id_str))\n    }\n\n    async fn add_dependency(&self, blocker_id: &BeadId, blocked_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let blocker = blocker_id.as_ref();\n        let blocked = blocked_id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"dep\", \"add\", blocked, blocker, \"--type\", \"blocks\"])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf dep add {blocked} {blocker} --type blocks failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn remove_dependency(&self, blocked_id: &BeadId, blocker_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let blocked = blocked_id.as_ref();\n        let blocker = blocker_id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"dep\", \"remove\", blocked, blocker])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf dep remove {blocked} {blocker} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn doctor_repair(&self) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n        let stdout = self\n            .run_bf(&[\"doctor\", \"--repair\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"bf doctor --repair failed\")?;\n        Ok(BrCliBeadStore::parse_doctor_output(&stdout))\n    }\n\n    async fn doctor_check(&self) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n        let stdout = self.run_bf(&[\"doctor\"]).await.context(\"bf doctor failed\")?;\n        Ok(BrCliBeadStore::parse_doctor_output(&stdout))\n    }\n\n    async fn full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let db_path = self.workspace.join(\".beads/beads.db\");\n\n        if db_path.exists() {\n            tokio::fs::remove_file(&db_path)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to remove {}\", db_path.display()))?;\n            tracing::info!(path = %db_path.display(), \"removed corrupt database file\");\n        }\n\n        for suffix in &[\"-wal\", \"-shm\"] {\n            let wal_path = tracing::info!(\"database fully rebuilt from JSONL — verified clean\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests return self.stop(&reason).await;\n                    }\n                    WorkerState::Stopped | WorkerState::Exhausted | WorkerState::Errored => {\n                        return
